Senses.Explanation: Green bamboo is presented in the records as immediately displaying or being the body, and that claim is then publicly challenged; the phrase is therefore a tested claim rather than scenery. Literally “verdant green bamboo.” In the Chan corpus these four ordinary landscape words are overwhelmingly the first half of a disputed stock proposition: “verdant green bamboo is entirely the true-as-is” or “entirely the body of reality,” paired with “luxuriant yellow flowers are none other than complete discernment” (青青翠竹，盡是真如／法身；鬱鬱黃花，無非般若). The proposition is not a settled glossary equation. The Ancestral Hall Collection explicitly records that some call it a wrong saying while others accept it; elsewhere in the same text one named record subject answers “it does not pervade form”, and Dazhu Huihai rejects identifying the bamboo itself with the body of reality. Dahui preserves both sides and describes Nanyang Huizhong as maintaining “verdant green bamboo is entirely the body of reality” while Dazhu breaks it as “verdant green bamboo is not the body of reality” (國師主張青青翠竹盡是法身；大珠破青青翠竹不是法身). The phrase also enters interviews: asked “verdant green bamboo is entirely the true-as-is; what is the true-as-is?”, a named record subject answers, “a guest who turns tile into gold—one hears the name but does not see the form” (點瓦成金客，聞名不見形); asked for “the wish-granting pearl that follows color,” another answers “verdant green bamboo, luxuriant yellow flowers” (青青翠竹，鬱鬱黃花). Thus Zen bends a landscape phrase into a repeatedly quoted proposition, dispute, and question-answer case; the record itself refuses one uncontested equation.
Senses.Note: #0g deviation: this is not merely bamboo scenery. It functions as the fixed opening of a proposition repeatedly affirmed, denied, questioned, and commented on by Chan teachers. The paired phrase “luxuriant yellow flowers” (鬱鬱黃花) has 57 hits in 41 texts. Exact “verdant green bamboo is entirely the body of reality” (青青翠竹盡是法身) has 18 hits in 14 texts. Headword count: 116 hits in 68 texts. “True-as-is” and “body of reality” translate the two attested predicates without adding a definition beyond these recorded predicates.
